lens: design concept, art direction, hierarchy and restraint vs ref-02

margins_css_px.verdict: FAIL: left 64 vs right 134 (about 19 mm difference). The bottom is covered by art, which is acceptable only as art space

axis.verdict: FAIL: the centred header sits about 9 mm off the axis of the left-weighted text block

columns.verdict: unequal widths; the 40 px end difference is absorbed by the art (acceptable)

measurements.left_edges: col1 all x 64, col2 all x 432: pass
measurements.grid: all 14 row tops are multiples of 8; Cocktails and Draft Beer share y 240: pass
measurements.header_spacing: one 32 px section gap, H2 16+8, H3 16 before: pass

price_pair_scan.verdict: pass; tabular figures, muted ink, no age-statement misreading

measurements.substitution_test: FAIL: a gold engraved agave on bottle green is ref-02 panel 3's palette and grammar, and it could run for any mezcal bar anywhere; only the sub-line says Iowa

remove: The dense heart-shading and hatched-cone fill in the lower-right corner. It turns into a solid gold slab with moire-like parallel hatching that competes with CANTINA for first read. Cut it back so the rosette reads as a line engraving, not a filled mass. A second candidate is the long overshooting outline whiskers at the leaf tips (for example the left-most leaf and the thin strokes above the Draft Beer column), which read as drawing errors.
top_problem: This is a competent copy of ref-02 panel 3 (same bottle-green and gold palette, same tracked CANTINA, same engraved-agave corner), not an ownable idea. The design admits it fails the substitution test. The boldest missing idea is a single gesture that fuses Mexico and Iowa City in the drawing itself, for example the agave rosette built from, or rising out of, one Iowa form that reads at a glance. Without that, criterion 15 cannot pass 60.
fixes: Make the concept ownable. Fuse the Iowa cue into the one gesture itself (the rosette's geometry, its ground line or its crop), not into a second drawing or the sub-line, and test it with the substitution test before building.
Re-centre the header on the text block's axis (x about 373) or set the whole page on one axis, and even out the side margins, which are now 64 px left against 134 px right on col 2 (about 19 mm off).

Replace the machine-regular parallel hatching and the overshooting outline whiskers with engraving-grade line work: tapering strokes and varied spacing, with no moire at print size. At actual size the rosette now reads as generated, not engraved, and falls below the painterly craft of ref-02 panels 1 and 5.
Rebalance the columns: widen col 2 to match col 1 (or narrow col 1) so the block is a true two-column grid, and let the art, not the unequal measure, carry the asymmetry.
Break away from the reference's colour recipe: bottle green plus gold is ref-02 panel 3 verbatim. Choose a ground and accent that belong to this venue's own thesis, keeping accent area at 8% or less.

lens: items and prices vs draft_doc.json, ingredient names and completeness (meta.public_components), flow
top_problem: Half the menu has no real descriptions. Cocktails get full spirit, modifier and garnish lines, but all 10 non-cocktail items print draft stubs that just repeat their names ('Blanco tequila pour', 'VSOP Cognac pour', 'Toasty amber lager', 'Dry red wine'). The page never says what is missing, and the Sparkling Brut Rosé has no glass or bottle label. So the spirits, beer, wine and cider sections read as filler next to a well-written cocktail block, and those categories are not treated equally.
problems: Content integrity passes. All 14 draft items are present with the draft's names and prices: Margarita 15, Manhattan 15, House Daiquiri 14, Brown Butter Old Fashioned 16, Blanco Tequila 12, Añejo Tequila 16, Cognac VSOP 18, Czech Pilsner 7, Dry-Hopped IPA 8, Amber Lager 7, Dry Cider 8, Malbec 12, Pinot Grigio 11, Brut Rosé 13. Nothing is invented or dropped. There are no taglines, prop captions or side-rail text.

The hidden component is handled correctly. Manhattan's meta.public_components marks aromatic-bitters as false, and the menu prints 'Rye whiskey · sweet vermouth · cocktail cherry' with no bitters. The garnishes (lime wheel, lime coin, orange peel, cocktail cherry) are cited to the recipe_versions rows f06abb74, 14d45e57, 7095fd3d and 9fb77eaa.

Brown Butter Old Fashioned has public_visibility.house_recipe set to false, yet the menu prints its full component chain as an ingredient list. The draft's own description names the same components, so no fact is exposed, but the flag should be confirmed with Rob.

Known gap, not counted against the designer: beer has no ABV, wine has no region and spirits have no brand or age detail. The designer flags this only in proposal.md, not in any on-menu or data flag, and the stubs repeat the item names. The two tequilas and the Cognac read as pure tautology.
Brut Rosé 13 sits under SPARKLING with no pour label. Malbec and Pinot Grigio get 'By the Glass', so the guest cannot tell whether 13 buys a glass or a bottle.

Descriptions do not share one voice. The Margarita runs a dot-list and then adds the draft sentence 'Bright and citrus-forward.' No other cocktail has a sensory line. The IPA description says 'draft' under a DRAFT BEER heading, which is redundant.

The sub-label hierarchy is inconsistent. Cocktails, Spirits and Wine show H3 sub-groups, but Draft Beer folds the draft's 'Draft' sub-group into its H2 and Cider has none. That changes how the draft's grouping reads.

The flow is logical for a cantina (Cocktails, then Agave and Brandy, then Draft Beer, Cider, Wine) and reads top to bottom, column 1 then column 2, with one clear entry at CANTINA. The cost: Spirits takes the second-strongest slot in column 1 with the thinnest content, and the long cocktail block is followed by three one-line stubs. Column 2 is only 250 px wide and ends pressed against the agave, so Wine, the last stop on the path, feels squeezed.

Inline prices sit 15 px after each name (4 to 6% eye travel) in tabular figures, with no $ and no decimals, and the format is consistent. Because they are inline, their x position varies row to row, so prices cannot be compared down a column, and wine has no pour-size column.
fixes: Ask Rob for a pour label (glass or bottle) for Brut Rosé 13, and print it as a matching sub-label or inline label next to 'By the Glass'.

Replace the name-repeating spirit, beer and wine stubs with flagged placeholders tied to data (for example 'ABV pending', 'region pending', 'house pour, brand pending') until Rob fills missing_ingredients, rather than printing 'Blanco tequila pour'-style tautologies.
Give all five sections the same sub-label logic: either show 'Draft' as an H3 under a 'Beer' H2, as the draft groups it, or drop H3s wherever a section has only one group.

Put the Margarita's 'Bright and citrus-forward.' on its own line in the same voice, or give every house cocktail a one-clause sensory line drawn only from known facts, so the cocktail descriptions share one voice.

Confirm with Rob that the Brown Butter Old Fashioned's house_recipe=false allows printing its component list. If it does not, fall back to the draft description 'Brown butter-washed bourbon, demerara, bitters' plus the orange peel garnish.

lens: ingredient/garnish/label traceability to build/draft_doc.json and phg.recipe_versions; description-price layout and price-to-item association in explore-I4/preview-letter.png
top_problem: Every printed fact traces to a source, but the copy does not read like a finished menu. Four cocktail lines are bare ingredient lists that run straight into their garnish (lime wheel, cocktail cherry, lime coin, orange peel read as ingredients). Only the Margarita gets a flavour sentence ('Bright and citrus-forward.'). The spirits descriptions only repeat the item name ('Blanco tequila pour', 'Añejo tequila pour', 'VSOP Cognac pour'). A Mexican cantina in Iowa City also shows no cantina-specific emphasis beyond the agave art. Verified sources: garnishes match phg.recipe_versions f06abb74 (Margarita, 'Lime wheel'), 9fb77eaa (Manhattan, 'Cocktail cherry'), 14d45e57 (House Daiquiri, 'Lime coin') and 7095fd3d (Brown Butter Old Fashioned, 'Orange peel'). The ingredients match the draft_doc components: Tequila Blanco, Fresh Lime Juice, Orange Liqueur, Agave Syrup; Rye Whiskey, Sweet Vermouth, with Aromatic Bitters correctly left off by public_components {'aromatic-bitters': false}; White Rum, Fresh Lime Juice, Demerara Syrup; Brown Butter-Washed Bourbon, Demerara Syrup, Aromatic Bitters. All 14 printed prices match phg.menu_items.menu_price (15/15/14/16/12/16/18/7/8/7/8/12/11/13). The beer, wine, cider and spirit descriptions are verbatim from menu_items.menu_description. 'Añejo' and 'Rosé' keep their accents as in the source. No tagline or caption states an item fact: the only non-item copy is 'CANTINA / & Cocktail Bar / Iowa City, Iowa'. Traceability gap: phg.menu_items for project ddc4bb5b now also holds 'Junmai Ginjo' at $12 ('Junmai Ginjo sake.'). It is not in build/draft_doc.json (revision 3, synced 2026-09-23) or the design. The design is faithful to its draft, but the draft is stale against the live project. Criterion 14: prices sit inline 15 px after each name (eye travel 4% in col 1 and 6% in col 2, measured in render_report.json), so association is unambiguous. However, the House Daiquiri line breaks to leave 'lime coin' alone on line 2. The Margarita's flavour sentence is tacked onto an ingredient string. Brut Rosé 13 has no pour label because the 'Sparkling' sub-label cuts it off from 'By the Glass'.
fixes: Set the garnish apart from the ingredient string (for example '… agave syrup; lime wheel' or a final 'garnished with lime coin'), citing the garnish column of recipe_versions f06abb74 / 9fb77eaa / 14d45e57 / 7095fd3d, and rebreak House Daiquiri so 'lime coin' does not sit alone on line 2.

Choose one description voice: either add a short sourced flavour clause to all four cocktails or drop 'Bright and citrus-forward.' from the Margarita, so it is no longer the only line with a sentence of voice.

Replace the name-echo spirit lines ('Blanco tequila pour', 'Añejo tequila pour', 'VSOP Cognac pour') with the type or age and region once Rob supplies brand, region and ABV, and flag them missing_ingredients in the proposal until then; do not ship them as final guest copy.
Give Brut Rosé 13 an explicit pour label (glass or bottle) from the inputs, or move 'Sparkling' under 'By the Glass' so its serve is not ambiguous.

Reconcile the draft with the live phg.menu_items: Junmai Ginjo ($12, 'Junmai Ginjo sake.') exists in project ddc4bb5b but not in build/draft_doc.json, so ask Rob whether it belongs on this menu and re-sync the draft before the next round.
